paper.title_en: Design of an electrostatic violin mode damper for gravitational wave detector enhancement
paper.abstract_en: The test mass suspension fiber resonances and their harmonics pollute the sensitivity of the detectors of the advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational Wave Observatory (aLIGO) and cause operational issues. The current method of damping these violin modes requires the GW detector be locked; identifying modes after a test mass replacement takes valuable commissioning time, and modes which are close together in frequency are hard to distinguish and damp independently. We present the design, prototyping, and initial lab testing of an electrostatic violin mode damper: a compact sensor and actuator set next to the fiber to monitor and damp resonances. The design uses a split photodiode and LED integrated into a shadow sensor, and an electrostatic actuator. The device is vacuum compatible and its mechanical design is compatible with the suspension and surrounding cage of the advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational Wave Observatory test masses. The shadow sensor has a shot noise limited displacement noise floor of 5e-11 {\meter\per√(\hertz)}, sufficient to measure the test mass violin modes when highly excited. The modeled actuator strength is 0.3 nN, meeting the requirements to damp the modes for the aLIGO suspensions.
